review_candidates.title: Information Technology Coordinator
review_candidates.description: Job Description Information Technology Coordinator What if your next role actually changed lives, including your own? At EF Language Abroad, we believe that learning a language abroad is one of the most transformative experiences a person can have. And we need passionate, driven people to help make that happen. That's where you come in. We're looking for an Information Technology Coordinator to join our team in Mexico City, Mexico . This is an entry level role for a curious, organized person who enjoys technology. You'll combine internal technical support with the automation of communication with customers and prospects, and you'll work closely with our IT operation, our Post Sales team, and demand generation. Your work will directly shape the experience of students and their families, from the first contact to their return from the program. No two days look the same, just meaningful work, real impact, and a team that's genuinely rooting for you from day one. Your Main Responsibilities IT Support and Operations (30%) Handle basic technical incidents for the Post Sales team and, when applicable, other areas. Manage user creation, removal, and permissions in the department's tools. Follow up on incidents with corporate IT and external vendors. Document processes, access, and configurations in step by step guides. Support the preparation and validation of equipment and tools for the area's operations. Customer Journey Automation (part of the 70%) Design, build, and maintain automated communication journeys for students and families: confirmations, document reminders, pre departure follow up, welcome messages, check ins during the program, and post program surveys. Configure email and SMS flows in the automation platform and in the CRM. Segment audiences by program type (APP, ILS, LT), destination, and journey stage. Monitor delivery, open, click, and conversion metrics, and propose improvements. Prospect Marketing Automation (part of the 70%) Build lead nurturing sequences, from the first inquiry to the close of the sale. Coordinate with the Sales and Marketing teams on lead management and qualification within the CRM. Support digital acquisition campaigns (email, social media, forms, and landing pages) in coordination with the central team. Keep contact databases clean and up to date, in compliance with privacy and consent policies. Continuous Improvement and Reporting Prepare simple performance reports on journeys and campaigns with clear indicators. Identify bottlenecks in Post Sales processes and propose automations that reduce them. Take part in testing new tools and improving existing flows. Requirements Education and Experience Bachelor's degree or technical degree in Systems, Computer Science, IT Engineering, Marketing, Digital Communication, or a related field (or student in the final semesters). 0 to 2 years of experience, preferably in technical support, internships, digital marketing, or automation. Languages Advanced English (B2 or above), spoken and written. Required to read technical documentation, work with central teams, and write communications in English for English speaking destinations. Native Spanish. Technical Knowledge Solid knowledge of Office tools, including intermediate Excel (pivot tables, basic formulas, and VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP). Medium to Advanced concepts of networks, operating systems, user directories, and incident resolution. Interest in, and basic experience with, marketing automation or CRM tools (HubSpot, Salesforce, or others). Basic knowledge of HTML/CSS or email builders is desirable. understanding of how AI is used in marketing and customer care (personalization, segmentation, automated responses). Skills Analytical thinking and results orientation. Organization and the ability to work with changing priorities between high and low season . About Us Some companies are in the business of banking. Others are in the business of shoes. Or sports. Or soft drinks. At EF, we're in a different kind of business. One that's a little less tangible, and a lot more important. Because our business, what we make, makes everything else possible. We're in the business of understanding. Between people. Between cultures. Through language, cultural exchange, academic studies, and educational travel, we create the kinds of immersive experiences that challenge biases, open minds, and pave the way for a more understanding world. You’ll find our offices and schools located in some of the world’s greatest cities, and filled with smart, driven people (over 50,000 of us) who push each other to be better every day. But it’s what we do together - building greater understanding, breaking down barriers, and creating a better world - that makes all the difference. Founded in 1965 in Sweden, EF (Education First) is a global association of education companies that share a common mission of opening the world through education. EF has been recognized on Forbes 2025 and 2024 World’s Best Employers and 2024 Top Companies for Women lists, Fast Company’s 2025 Next Big Things In Tech, and was a 2024 App Store Award winner in Cultural Impact. Since 1965, we've helped millions of students discover new places, embrace diverse cultures, and gain fresh perspectives. We're dedicated to our mission of opening the world through education, harnessing the power of language learning to deepen the connection between people across the globe. We offer immersive short-term and long-term language courses and programs across different languages in the countries where they’re spoken. Through blending classroom-based lessons with interactive exercises and real-world practice, our courses bring you to the heart of the language. Together, our global staff help students from around the world develop the language skills they need to achieve their dreams. EF is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. All positions are subject to a criminal background and/or reference checks, as applicable.

review_candidates.description: Overview The Implementation Research and Learning Advisor will provide technical expertise in Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) including a focus on implementation research to ensure delivery of high-quality technical approaches that reflect current best practices, with a focus on cancers including breast, cervical, and lung cancers. They will ensure technical approaches are aligned with and responsive to organizational, client and donor MERL and research needs and requirements. The Implementation Research and Learning Advisor will work with teams to define and determine the requirements for work, establishing actionable plans that support the conduct of implementation research and learning within programs. The Implementation Research and Learning Advisor will represent Jhpiego externally and establish strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders to advance organizational objectives. They will foster new relationships internally and support the development of new external partnerships to achieve objectives. The Implementation Research and Learning Advisor will build capacity, support knowledge sharing, and business development and will support the development and implementation of implementation research, selected work-plan activities and contribute to program learning. This position is open to candidates based in any Jhpiego country office, with East or Southeast Africa as the preferred locations. Responsibilities Technical Assistance & Quality Programming (75%) Provides quality technical assistance in design, implementation, and dissemination of implementation research and learning initiatives. Drawing on experience and technical knowledge, designs or adapts technical approaches based on team capacities, analysis of program data, stakeholder needs and changes in context or environment. For implementation research this includes protocol design, implementation planning, data analysis, reporting and dissemination, and data compliance. For programmatic learning this includes MEL plan development, systems design, staffing/coaching support, data review and use, data quality assurance, reporting support, and data compliance. Required Qualifications Advanced degree in public health (international health, epidemiology, biostatistics, population), statistics, research, economics, behavioural science, or related field. 7 years of progressively responsible technical experience including managing implementation research and MERL for programs in multiple countries where they are based and/or remotely. Experience with implementation research ideally including within non-communicable diseases (NCDs) programs, and/or cancers, and with using quantitative and qualitative methods. Preferred Qualifications Experience working or living in a low- or middle-income country. Knowledge And Skills Strong technical and programmatic background in MERL, especially technical support and in NCDs, ideally cancers. Implementation research study design and analysis, including development and use of theoretical frameworks. Quantitative data analysis, ideally including multilevel modelling, time-series analysis, or econometrics and/or comparable qualitative data analysis expertise. Strong knowledge of performance monitoring and data use for performance improvement. Experience in developing MERL systems for projects and country programs, ideally including those supporting NCDs. Knowledge of health information systems. Designing and conducting program evaluations. Proven leadership skills and expertise in strategic program planning, implementation, and management. Proven technical experience in the design, implementation, or measurement of technical interventions in NCDs, preferably including cancers. Proven experience in leading highly skilled and qualified technical personnel. Proven collaborator with ability to see and create connections across vertical health areas, as well as across functional areas. Understanding of donor systems, expectations, and processes, e.g. Unitaid, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. Proven ability and excellent experience developing productive working relationships with counterparts in other agencies and organizations worldwide. Excellent interpersonal and cross-cultural skills including the ability to communicate technical content verbally, in writing and through dynamic presentations. Team player who is comfortable working in a dynamic and evolving environment. Proficient oral and written English language skills; Multi language fluency required. PHYSICAL DEMANDS Ability to travel up to 25% time. Total compensation will be based on the country of hire and Jhpiego’s local compensation plan. review_candidates.title: IDB Invest Lead Investment Officer - Mobilization & Asset Sharing
review_candidates.description: We improve lives The IDB Group is a community of diverse, versatile, and passionate people who come together on a journey to improve lives in Latin America and the Caribbean. Our people find purpose and do what they love in an inclusive, collaborative, agile, and rewarding environment. IDB Invest is the private sector arm of the IDB Group and an international financial institution committed to addressing the development needs of Latin America and the Caribbean. Our mission is to support sustainable enterprises and projects that deliver financial results while maximizing social and environmental impact in the region. IDB Invest operates in 26 countries, structured across four geographic regions and three industry verticals: Infrastructure and Energy, Financial Intermediaries, and Corporates. In support of a new transformative business model “Originate to Share” our shareholders recently approved a $3.5 billion capitalization. This will allow IDB Invest to significantly scale up its investments, to approximately $19 billion, and unlock greater private sector participation to drive development and climate impact across the region. About This Position We are seeking dynamic and experienced Lead Investment Officers to join the Mobilization & Asset Sharing Division. The candidate should be an experienced banker with deep expertise in the structuring of debt products—including syndicated loans, B Loans, B Bonds, project finance, and other credit instruments—that are broadly distributed in the market, and a demonstrated ability to build and maintain strong relationships with clients, investors, and internal stakeholders that will contribute to the scaling up of the mobilization of assets. The Lead Investment Officer is a senior professional responsible for embedding mobilization and distribution considerations in the origination, structuring, and placement of IDB Invest’s transactions within their respective geography. Depending on the post of duty, this role will report to either the Director – Distribution & Investor Relations, the Director – Syndications Origination, or have dual reporting to both, based on the strategic priorities, deal flow, and market dynamics of each hub. To align with the Originate to Share business model, this role serves as a regional anchor for the Mobilization & Asset Sharing Division across Latin America and the Caribbean, working closely with Delivery Units, clients, and the investor community in the region. The Lead Investment Officer will play a critical role in scaling up mobilization volumes, deepening investor engagement, and positioning IDB Invest as a market leader in the origination and distribution of marketable development finance assets in Brazil, the Andean region, and Mexico and Central America, respectively. On this vacancy we are looking to fill three positions. What You’ll Do Support the Directors in the development and implementation of the mobilization and asset sharing strategy in the region, aligning initiatives with IDB Invest’s Originate to Share business model and mobilization targets. Serve as the primary point of reference for investment teams in the region on how to structure transactions with an eye toward distribution, ensuring that assets are originated with market parameters that facilitate the mobilization of third-party capital. Act as a focal point syndicated debt transactions in the region, advising on optimal terms, pricing, tenor, covenants, and documentation standards to maximize the attractiveness of IDB Invest’s assets across the full suite of mobilization products, including A/B Loans, B Bonds (Private Placement and 144A), Syndicated Co-financings, Unfunded Credit Protection, Unfunded Risk Participations, and Managed Accounts. Build and maintain strong, trusted relationships with clients (corporate borrowers, financial institutions, and infrastructure sponsors) and with local, regional, and international investors, including commercial and investment banks, asset managers, insurance companies, pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, DFIs, and impact investors. Lead the execution of primary and secondary distribution efforts in the region, including sell-down processes, in close coordination with origination and portfolio management teams. Provide market intelligence, structuring advice, and pricing guidance to origination teams, drawing on deep knowledge of the syndicated loan and local capital markets, investor appetite, and comparable transaction benchmarks to inform credit committee presentations and investment decision memoranda. Conduct investor roadshows, one-on-one meetings, and targeted outreach programs with local and regional investors to deepen market understanding of IDB Invest’s value proposition, Preferred Creditor Status, and product offerings. Lead the preparation of syndication strategies, term sheets, information memoranda, teasers, investor presentations, and other marketing materials required to support the primary and secondary distribution of IDB Invest’s assets. Champion the continuous development and adaptation of mobilization products to address local market conditions, including local currency structures, risk-transfer instruments, and portfolio-level solutions relevant to the region. Contribute to the coverage of specific investor accounts and industry verticals as part of the division’s global coverage model, ensuring consistent engagement and knowledge sharing across geographies. Promote knowledge sharing by disseminating market best practices, representing the division in internal and external forums, and contributing to the development of new origination and distribution frameworks and product governance processes. What You'll Need Education: Master’s degree (or equivalent advanced degree) in finance, business administration, economics, international development, or other fields relevant to the responsibilities of the role. Experience At least 6 years (10 Years desirable) of relevant professional experience in loan syndications, debt structuring, debt distribution, capital markets, or structured finance at an international financial institution, commercial or investment bank, asset management firm, multilateral development bank, or other private sector entity is required. Experience at the Vice President or Director level in syndications origination, distribution, or capital markets teams is highly desirable. Deep experience in the structuring of debt products (loans and bonds)—including syndicated loans, B Loans, and bond placements (private placement and 144A)—that are broadly distributed in the market, with a proven track record of originating, executing, and placing transactions. Demonstrated ability to build and maintain strong relationships with clients, investors, and internal stakeholders (investment officers, structuring teams, legal, risk management, and treasury) that will contribute to the scaling up of the mobilization of assets. Experience working in a fast-paced, transaction-oriented environment. Experience working in an international financial organization, large corporate, or similar institution is highly desired. Experience operating within complex organizations that balance multiple objectives is a requirement. Familiarity with LSTA documentation, participation agreements, and syndicated credit structures. Knowledge of unfunded credit instruments and risk-transfer products considered a plus. Knowledge of local debt capital and syndications markets in Brazil, the Andean region, or Mexico and Central America is a must. Working knowledge of the following technologies and areas would be considered a plus: Bloomberg, Debt Domain, CRM platforms, Power BI. Languages: Proficiency in English is required and one of the other Bank official languages (Spanish if based in the Andean or Central America Regions or Portuguese if based in Sao Paulo, Brazil). Requirements Citizenship: No requirements. Consanguinity: You have no family members (up to the fourth degree of consanguinity and second degree of affinity, including spouse) working at the IDB, IDB Invest, or IDB Lab. Type of contract and duration National or TCN: National or Third Country National, 36 months initially, renewable upon mutual agreement. Please note that the applicable contract will be determined by the IDB Group. This determination will be based on the location of the position, as well as the selected candidate’s nationality, residency status, and/or authorization to work without the need for sponsorship of the IDB Group in the country of assignment. What We Offer The IDB group provides benefits that respond to the different needs and moments of an employee's life. These benefits include: A competitive compensation package Leaves and vacations: 24 days of paid time off + 8 personal days + sick leave + gender-neutral parental leave Health Insurance: IDB Group provides employees and eligible dependents with a robust medical benefits program that covers medical, dental, vision, preventive care, and prescription drugs. Pension plan: defined benefit pension plan that provides financial security and support employees in planning for their future. On-site position with the occasional flexibility of teleworking. Health and well-being: Access to our Health Services Center that provides preventive care and health education for employees. Development support: We offer tools to boost your professional profile, such as mentoring, 1:1 professional counseling, training and learning opportunities, language classes, mobility options, among others. Our culture At the IDB, we work so everyone brings their best and authentic selves to work while finding their purpose. Our people consistently strive for excellence, and we recognize and celebrate the impact of their contributions. In our efforts to drive innovation, we intentionally include all voices, cultivate a sense of belonging and champion fairness. We welcome individuals from underrepresented groups to join us and share their unique perspectives. We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job interview process. If you require an accommodation to complete this application, please email us at accommodations@iadb.org. #IDBInvest

HJF is seeking a Deputy Director - Research & Analysis to support the National Institute for Defense Health Cooperation (NIDHC), a center of the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences (USU) in Bethesda, MD. The R&A Deputy Director will serve as both an action officer and co-director to the R&A Director. This individual will contribute to and execute a vision with NIDHC leadership that strategically aligns capabilities by supervising and growing scientific staff and managing an applied research project portfolio while simultaneously determining the feasibility of applying and scaling approaches and concepts. The Deputy Director will serve as Co-Principal Investigator and is responsible for independently conceiving, designing, and adapting complex research projects that address military and civilian health enterprise gaps in coordination with NIDHC leadership and interagency partners. Effective leadership of the R&A Directorate may include initiating funding opportunities across the military and civilian health enterprise. The incumbent will directly support the Military-Civilian Health Ecosystem, which is a network of academic, not-for-profit, government, and industry partners that support NIDHC and the federal interagency to conduct science, carryout operational research, and develop training and education for advancing the practice of medicine and public health in crisis and conflict. Launched in October 2025, NIDHC supports military and civilian health operational readiness in crisis and conflict, both domestically and internationally. Formed by merging the strengths of the National Center for Disaster Medicine and Public Health (NCDMPH), the Center for Global Health Engagement (CGHE), and the security cooperation education and training functions of the Defense Institute for Medical Operations (DIMO), NIDHC serves as a powerful hub for advancing defense health cooperation. Through its four core capabilities – Program Leadership, Training & Education, Research & Analysis, and Planning & Partnership – the Institute directly supports national priorities by focusing on enhancing military readiness, health security, civil-military cooperation, and international partnerships. The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government partners by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals. Responsibilities Lead the planning, execution, and oversight of research projects and protocols, including delegation to scientific and technical staff. Work with program staff to manage projects, track funding, and ensure appropriate administrative actions (e.g., institutional review board compliance). Vet funding opportunities for relevance, eligibility, and strategy alignment. Brainstorm with and enable program staff to strategically partner and maximize research and project opportunities, both scientifically and financially. Work with program staff and Ecosystem partners to ensure quality, cost, and timelines are maintained. Supervise, mentor, and coach scientific staff. Coordinate and prepare new funding applications. Make major contributions to scientific literature and conferences. Envision and prepare publication-ready manuscripts. Review and finalize scientific knowledge products for symposia, conferences, and journals. Engage with the leaders of the Military Civilian Medical Surge Program (MCMSP), Global Health Engagement programs, Pre and Post-Crash Care Programs, and Ecosystem projects to identify new directions, shepherd opportunities, and create connections between partner organizations. Co-develop a R&A Directorate strategy; roadmap and implement operational plans relative to strategies. Understand and promote the Ecosystem and NIDHC with current and new partners as well as interagency stakeholders. Support NIDHC leadership in senior level engagements across government, academia, and industry. Serve as in-house and outside technical consultant. May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the supervisor. This may include attendance of and participation in required training for the role. Initiate, develop, and communicate new applied research and implementation proposals, projects, and protocols based on basic and early research findings. Simultaneously direct and manage matrixed staff, external subcontracted teams, support staff, and students/interns on integrated and discrete projects and initiatives. Execute, grow, and sustain the R&A Directorate with little prompting or supervision. Assess issues to determine urgency and articulate and disseminate clear, timely decisions in the best interests of NIDHC.
